title: USDA, undeterred by judge’s stay, moves ‘full-bore ahead’ with reorganization steps
summary: The Agriculture Department is still carrying out reorganization activities not explicitly barred by a judge’s stay.

title: Bureau of Prisons seeks another shot at ending union contracts
summary: One union local president said he is still routinely denied official time, has meeting requests ignored, and that his prison has failed to reinstitute compressed work schedules.

title: The legal fight over the public service student loan forgiveness overhaul may be over
summary: Two different federal judges in June ruled that the Education Department’s changes to the program were unlawful. On Wednesday, the Trump administration dropped its appeals.

title: These former feds could be members of Congress next year
summary: Most of these candidates face long odds of winning or are in tight races.

title: CDC hiring plan and more permanent leadership coming soon, director tells staff
summary: CDC leaders say they're close to finishing a hiring plan that would replenish the agency’s ranks after deep staffing cuts last year, but employees have heard similar messages since March 2026.

title: If you already have FEHB, should you sign up for Medicare B?
summary: Pairing your federal health plan with Medicare can lower out-of-pocket costs, but monthly premiums and income-based surcharges add up. Here’s what to consider before deciding whether the extra coverage is worth the price.

title: DOGE’s layoffs took a toll on Black women. The effects are still being felt
summary: The loss of federal jobs has left many Black women grappling with financial insecurity, emotional distress and an uncertain future, with consequences that extend beyond the workplace.

title: Instagram, comic books and public engagement: One watchdog’s plan to protect inspector general independence
summary: Lucy Lang, the inspector general for New York state, argued in an interview with Government Executive that IGs should prioritize improving the public’s trust in government — both through investigations and making sure citizens know that oversight is happening.

title: HHS telework rollback challenge upheld by FLRA
summary: Federal Labor Relations Authority members wrote that HHS seemingly used generative AI tools to draft its legal brief, since many of its citations were “fictitious, erroneous, or irrelevant.”

title: ‘Last chance to stay where you are.’ USDA gives some employees facing relocation a shot at unfilled local jobs
summary: A Natural Resources Conservation Service employee said most critical vacancies available at his grade level would amount to a "voluntary downgrade," but would spare him from relocating across the country.

title: ‘It’s The Price is Right’: How USCIS artificially deflated employee ratings under forced distribution mandate
summary: A federal whistleblower says the agency instituted a forced distribution of employee performance ratings last year, months before the Trump administration lifted a ban on the practice.

title: USPTO looks to AI agents to ease examiner workloads
summary: The office’s Acting Commissioner for Patents Barry Schindler said putting agents in the hands of its examiners “can shorten that [review process] to one year, because you can pick up the phone and have conversations.”

title: ICE wants AI to take on more of its legal workload
summary: The agency is looking for software that can help its attorneys manage the growing demands of litigation, investigations and other legal matters.

title: ‘A rushed and complicated system.’ Federal employees say they’re in the dark over limited top ratings
summary: A mandate to limit outstanding performance scores has managers playing a numbers game and risks pitting teammates against each other.

title: Oversight of nuclear material security cut back due to civil service reductions, GAO finds
summary: The Government Accountability Office also reported that the National Nuclear Security Administration has more than lost its recent hiring gains.

title: State Department orders ‘super intelligence’ wording across all official communications
summary: An internal cable from the agency extends Trump’s terminology change to emails, speeches, websites and official titles, while preserving legal language and historical records.

title: Trump’s IG pick at the VA is ‘watering down’ oversight, some employees allege
summary: As the Veterans Affairs inspector general faces mounting workforce challenges, some employees and former watchdogs raise questions about the office's trajectory.

title: Union seeks new avenue to restore VA contract
summary: The American Federation of Government Employees asked a federal judge to issue an “indicative” ruling that would only take effect if OKed by the First Circuit Court of Appeals.

title: This cybersecurity agency is supposed to protect U.S. elections. Officials fear it’s been compromised by Trump
summary: President Donald Trump’s 2027 budget proposal would reduce funding for the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency by another $700 million, which could necessitate 900 additional layoffs.

title: Senator warns hundreds of federal web addresses may lack key spying protection
summary: The list includes websites for FBI tips, intelligence job applications and the Veterans Crisis Line.

title: Enforcement ‘surge’ from DOJ, IRS uncovers $490M in suspected tax fraud
summary: Justice and IRS officials said this won’t be the last tax fraud enforcement surge of its kind. But it's not yet clear how much money they'll claw back from suspected fraudsters.

title: Judge again orders reinstatement of Bureau of Prisons union contracts, but stops short of contempt
summary: U.S. District Judge Jordan Oliver found that the agency’s re-termination of its collective bargaining agreements last week violated last month’s preliminary injunction but said he would not police individual contract infractions.

title: VA allows union contract to expire for most employees
summary: Individuals hired as departmental police officers, firefighters and security guards, exempted from Trump’s anti-union orders, remain covered under the expired collective bargaining agreement, albeit only for “mandatory” conditions of employment.

title: USPS ‘ready to deliver’ ballots in midterms without mail-in voting EO restrictions
summary: The Postal Service's law enforcement agency is investigating suspicious letters sent to several state officials who oversee election operations.
